subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should OpenClaw add recurring native PowerShell smoke coverage for both `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke`, or start with a narrower proven command set?
rationale: The direction fits test-infrastructure priorities, but current PR evidence shows one proposed command is not yet safe in the target Windows lane and the recurring runner cost is a maintainer scope choice.

options.title: Prove the full smoke before merge
options.body: Keep both requested commands, but merge only after the exact Windows `pwsh` lane passes and the PR includes redacted successful proof for that final command set.

options.title: Start narrower
options.body: Land only native PowerShell commands that already pass, then track heavier build-smoke coverage separately once it is Windows-safe.

options.title: Defer recurring CI coverage
options.body: Keep the issue open as a planning item and pause the PR until runner budget or release priorities justify the lane.

recommendation.title: Prove the full smoke before merge
recommendation.body: Keep both requested commands, but merge only after the exact Windows `pwsh` lane passes and the PR includes redacted successful proof for that final command set.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent overlap across the CI workflow and the PowerShell-safe docs formatter that the smoke lane would exercise.
